subject: Emergency headroom request for late-night latency soak
messages:
From: Asha Gupta <asha@fastretail.io>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fastretail.io>, procure@fastretail.io
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: urgent headroom for overnight latency soak (tonight)

Hi Irene —

Quick note from the FastRetail ops team: we kicked off a preliminary overnight soak in our staging cluster this morning and are seeing intermittent tail-latency spikes when we move beyond ~6k concurrent requests. The team would like to run a focused 6h overnight soak tonight (midnight–6am PT) that pushes to 12k concurrent to validate the latency profile under sustained QPS.

Can Redwood provide an emergency trial credit bump (ephemeral headroom) to cover the extra tokens/throughput for tonight's run? We don't expect persistent usage after the soak — this is strictly a one-time test to finalize capacity planning for the paid Dedicated evaluation.

I've attached the soak plan and a short log excerpt. Key asks:
- Temporary allowance for ~48M tokens or equivalent throughput for 6h
- A brief contact for infra fallback if errors spike (Slack preferred)

Thanks — really appreciate the quick help here.

— Asha
Asha Gupta
Sr. SRE, FastRetail
Attachment: fastretail-night-soak-plan.csv (attachment); staging-latency-sample.log (attachment)

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Asha Gupta <asha@fastretail.io>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@fastretail.io>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: urgent headroom for overnight latency soak (tonight)

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the details and for attaching the plan. Short answer: we can support a one-off buffer, but need to coordinate approval and a mutual action plan so we can monitor and have fallbacks ready.

Proposed quick plan:
1) Approve ephemeral headroom: 50M token allowance, valid for 6h tonight (00:00–06:00 PT)
2) Monitoring hook: our on-call (Jonas) joins your Slack #fastretail-ops channel at 23:45 PT for a warm handoff
3) Fallback policy: if 5xx errors >2% for 10m or p95 latency >1.8s, we’ll automatically throttle or redirect to the lighter q4 model variant
4) Post-run follow-up: short postmortem and cost summary tomorrow morning

Can you confirm the exact start time your team will flip the load generator and who will own the run from your side? If you confirm now I’ll route the credit approval to Marissa for sign-off.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: none

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: urgent headroom for overnight latency soak (tonight)

Filed quick read of the logs Asha sent — thanks. A few notes from infra:
- The p95 spikes correlate with long seq lengths in a small subset of requests; recommending an enforced max_seq of 512 for the soak to reduce variance
- We can enable prefix KV caching for repeated prefixes (should reduce token compute by ~8–12%)
- I’ll be on Slack tonight and can flip the model variant fallback if we see sustained errors

Operational checklist for tonight (Irene / Asha / Jonas):
- Confirm start time (Asha)
- Confirm who will own throttles on FR side (Sam?)
- I’ll post a short runbook in the Drive link and pin to Slack

— Jonas

Subject: Re: Request: urgent headroom for late-night latency soak — run complete

Hi all —

Run completed at 05:58 PT. Quick summary:
- We pushed to peak ~11.6k concurrent, 6h duration
- p95 stayed under 1.6s after enforcing max_seq=512 and enabling prefix caching
- Token usage: ~41.3M (within the 50M allowance)
- No sustained 5xx periods; a short 7-minute blip at 02:14 resolved after a quick throttle on our side

Next steps:
- We'll share the full postmortem and graphs in the Drive link by 09:00 PT
- Procure will follow up on any reconciliation items if needed

Huge thanks to Jonas and Marissa for the quick enable — this was critical in validating our capacity assumptions.

— Asha
Sr. SRE, FastRetail
Attachment: none
